change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a user-controlled negative offset
findings.body: `Cursor.from_string` accepts any integer for the offset (`src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:59`), so `?cursor=0:-5:0` reaches `queryset[-5:stop]` at line 882. The comment says Django handles negative slicing, but Django querysets reject negative indexing with an AssertionError, so the request returns a 500. The 'advanced' path therefore cannot work for the offsets it was written for. If it did work it would bypass the intended bounds of cursor pagination, as the comment 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' admits. The comment 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' does not make arbitrary offsets safe. Remove the negative-offset branch. If the goal is faster reverse pagination, reject negative offsets in cursor parsing (a 400) and use the existing `is_prev` mechanism.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator behaviour changed for every endpoint, and the comment contradicts the code
findings.body: `BasePaginator.get_result` is used by all `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` endpoints. Before, a negative offset reached the slice unchanged. Now, for `is_prev=False`, `max(0, offset)` silently turns a negative offset into 0 and returns page 1 instead of an error. For `is_prev=True` the negative offset still reaches the slice and raises. The comment says negative offsets are now 'allowed', but the code clamps them (non-prev) or leaves the old failure (prev). This change is unrelated to the PR title and has no test. Revert it, or validate the offset explicitly and add tests.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` is Optional and is dereferenced on every request by non-superusers
findings.body: `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (`src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346`). Line 71 runs for every GET, not only when `optimized_pagination=true`. For a non-superuser caller with no member row (for example an org-scoped token), it raises AttributeError and returns a 500 on the previously working default path. Compute `enable_advanced` only inside `if use_optimized`, and guard against `member is None`.

findings.title: Uses `request.user.is_superuser` instead of `is_active_superuser(request)`
findings.body: Other org endpoints gate superuser behaviour with `is_active_superuser(request)` (`src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:70,124,304`), which also checks the active superuser session. `user.is_superuser` is only the account flag, so a superuser without an active session passes this gate. Use `is_active_superuser`. Also, an undocumented `optimized_pagination` query flag that unlocks a different cursor code path is a new public-API behaviour with no tests.

findings.title: Audit-log paginator change is unrelated to the PR (spans buffer eviction)
findings.body: The PR title and body describe only 'spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert'. The audit-log endpoint, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the `BasePaginator` change and the `Cursor` comment have nothing to do with that. Please split them out into a separate PR. They change the behaviour of a sensitive audit-log endpoint and of a paginator shared across the app, and they have no tests.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result wholesale
findings.body: The class subclasses `BasePaginator` but redefines `get_item_key` (identical to `Paginator`), `value_from_cursor` and a ~65-line `get_result` that differs only in the negative-offset branch at lines 877-882. The `else` branch is a duplicate of the base logic. Any future fix to the base will not reach it. The `Paginator` base is also wrong for the `datetime` key used by the audit log: `getattr(item, 'datetime')` is a `datetime`, so `math.floor(value)` raises TypeError and `value_from_cursor` returns a raw int that is compared against a datetime column. With `order_by='-datetime'` the optimized path fails on any page with results.

findings.title: Redirect-depth limit lowered 10000 → 1000 with the explanatory comment removed
findings.body: This is an unrelated, unexplained behaviour change. Trees deeper than 1000 are not joined correctly, and the loop gives up silently. Previously the limit was 10000 and documented. Restore it or justify it in the PR, and keep a comment.

findings.title: Eviction drops the oldest spans silently, replacing the old 'skip oversized segment, log error' behaviour
findings.body: `zpopmin` removes the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` entries once the set exceeds 1000. Segments that previously were flagged (error log and `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric) and skipped are now truncated with no log or metric. The oldest spans are typically the earliest children, and the root span can end last, so truncation silently loses data from segments sent downstream. The check in `buffer.py` was removed and `max_segment_spans` (`src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150,158`) is now an unused parameter. The 1000 is hard-coded in Lua and disconnected from it. Return the evicted count from the script and emit a metric, and pass the limit as an ARGV, or drop the dead parameter.

findings.title: zunionstore default SUM aggregation corrupts scores for duplicate members, and the deploy hits SET-typed keys
findings.body: (1) `ZUNIONSTORE` without `AGGREGATE` sums scores. A payload present in both source keys (a redelivered Kafka message, or the same payload zadd'ed under both keys) gets a doubled timestamp, so it is evicted later than newer spans. Use `AGGREGATE MIN`/`MAX` explicitly. (2) Segment keys written by the previous version are Redis SETs with a TTL of `redis_ttl` (3600s). On a rolling deploy, `zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zscan` on such a key returns WRONGTYPE, which fails the pipeline in `process_spans` and `_load_segment_data`. Old and new consumers also share keys during the rollout. Plan a migration, such as a key-name version bump, or document that the buffer must be drained first.

findings.title: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError if the field is absent
findings.body: Other fields are read with `val[...]`, but a missing or `None` timestamp in a single span now fails the whole batch in `process_batch`, and the consumer crashes. If the schema marks `end_timestamp_precise` as required, this is fine. Otherwise handle it, for example by falling back to the Kafka message timestamp. The `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` only silences the type checker and does not validate.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction, zset ordering or paginator behaviour
findings.body: The test changes only add `end_timestamp_precise` to existing spans, and every span uses the same timestamp (1700000000.0). Nothing tests: eviction above 1000 spans (which spans are dropped), the Lua span_count paths (set_key merged with span_key and parent_key), or the removed too-many-spans behaviour. Identical scores also mean ordering is never exercised. Nothing tests `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the `optimized_pagination` flag, or the `BasePaginator` offset change. Add tests with distinct timestamps and a segment over 1000 spans.

contracts.action: Span payloads stored as sorted set members scored by end_timestamp_precise; Lua merges via ZUNIONSTORE and evicts via ZPOPMIN above 1000
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous SADD/SUNIONSTORE path in the same script, plus the segment_span_count_exceeded check in _load_segment_data, which skipped oversized segments with an error log
contracts.before_after: Before: unbounded set, with oversize detected at flush and the segment skipped with a log and metric. After: size capped at insert, oldest spans silently dropped. SET keys from old consumers cause WRONGTYPE.
contracts.visible_effect: Segments over 1000 spans are flushed truncated with no error signal. Downstream segment processing sees incomplete traces.
contracts.failure_mode: WRONGTYPE ResponseError on existing SET keys during rollout fails the pipeline and the consumer. Duplicate payload scores are summed.

contracts.action: Audit-log GET optionally uses OptimizedCursorPaginator when optimized_pagination=true for superuser or global-access members
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing DateTimePaginator path in the same endpoint, and BasePaginator.get_result
contracts.before_after: Before: always DateTimePaginator. After: the request evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access on every call, and the opt-in path uses Paginator-style integer keys on a datetime column and passes negative offsets to the queryset slice.
contracts.visible_effect: A 500 for a negative cursor offset on the optimized path. Possible 500 for requests with no member on the default path. A 500 on the optimized path whenever results exist (floor of datetime).
contracts.failure_mode: AttributeError (member None), AssertionError (negative slice), TypeError (math.floor on datetime).

summary: The spans-buffer ZSET/eviction change has real problems: oversized segments are now silently truncated, existing SET keys will fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, `max_segment_spans` is now dead, and no test covers the new behaviour. The PR also carries an unrelated audit-log and paginator change that does not match its title. That change does not work: Django rejects the negative offset slice, so those requests return a 500. It also dereferences a possibly-None `member` on the default path, uses `user.is_superuser` rather than `is_active_superuser`, and alters the shared `BasePaginator`. The blocker is the negative-offset path in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`.
